newsitem.title: USA: Dow seen higher at open, chip stocks seen firm.
newsitem.headline: Dow seen higher at open, chip stocks seen firm.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to open higher on Tuesday, boosted by new evidence of improving conditions in the semiconductor industry.

The Semiconductor Industry Association reported late Monday that its book-to-bill ratio, which measures new orders against shipments, rose to 1.15 in November, a better than expected improvement from October's revised 1.11 reading.
"Chip stocks are higher in Europe and that should help the market get off to a good start," said Larry Wachtel, market analyst at Prudential Securities.
The strong reading was released after the close of a session that saw the Dow industrials rise 82 points, undoing their losses from last Friday's session and apparently regaining their momentum.

"This market is not going to give up that easily," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments. "I thought we'd get a bit of selling pressure yesterday but the reverse happened."
"The market has entered a momentum stage," he said.
Investors will be treated to a flurry of economic information today, including key weekly retail sales data.
First up is the BTM-Schroders report on chain store sales for the week ended December 7, due at 0900 EST/1400 GMT. The weekly Redbook report is due at 1455 EST/1955 GMT.

Also due today are reports on wholesale inventories for October, the U.S. current account for the third quarter and the November Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond survey of business conditions, all scheduled for release at 1000 EST/1500 GMT.
U.S. Treasuries edged lower ahead of the data, with the 30-year bond off a quarter of a point to yield 6.48 percent.
In Tokyo, stocks registered strong gains, led by high tech shares. The Nikkei-225 index gained 218 points to 20,822.
Chip stocks led U.S. shares higher in London. The FTSE-100 rose 25 points to 4036.6.
The dollar was firmer in Tokyo, rising to about 113.6 yen, but eased to stand at about 1.55 marks and 113.2 yen after failing to crack resistance in Europe.
The December Standard & Poor's 500 index future rose 1.9 points to 753.3.

The New York Times Marketplace column examines a strategy employed by Guy Wyser-Pratte in a proxy fight against the board of Rexene Corp. Wyser-Pratte's nominees to the Rexene board were all recruited by an executive search firm, the column reports, a departure from the common practice of nominating friends or colleagues to a dissident slate.

The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column reports that some investors are beginning to question the strong rally recently posted by bank stocks and wondering if the shares are finally hitting their upside limits.
